newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly weaker, gasoline steady.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly weaker, gasoline steady.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weaker on Wednesday but gasoline prices held steady.
Naphtha was slightly weaker with a a Skikda cargo on offer from an end user at flat or higher to the Algerian formula, with buyers holding out for a deep discount, traders said.
Freight rates had moved to high enough levels to discourage shipping the cargo to northwest Europe, they said.
A full range Suez cargo was still on offer at $226-227 cif NWE with buyers at $224.
"It's still there but I don't think there is any interest from the end users," a trader said.
Cargoes in the Med were quoted off $1 to $221/$223 cif.
Gasoline prices, bucking the weakness in crude and gas oil, held steady after U.S. inventory data showed a drop in gasoline supplies for last week.
Gas oil slid lower as underlying futures tumbled $6 a tonne, draining activity from the market by closing the arb to northern Europe and the Arabian Gulf.
"The whole Med is dead," one trader said.
Premiums were unchanged, with Russian notionally at cif high quotes +$1.50/1.75 cif Genoa for early November, with the differential to low sulphur diesel unchanged at around +$17.

Low sulphur cracked fuel oil markets were around $1 a tonne weaker. An Italian utility bought a 25,000 prompt cargo from a trader. The deal was agreed half at a fixed price of $130 cif NWE, and half at on a floating price based on the published quotes of two reporting services.

A Turkish tender to buy 25-50,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil was re-issued. The new tender specifies density of 0.975, and invites bids based on high sulphur quotes, and not on low sulphur quotes as was the case in the original tender.
A low sulphur tender, closing on Wednesday, was not altered.
